en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Mind of All Buddhas, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time the Bhagavān was dwelling in the Tathāgata-realm, the Hall of Many Jewels.
It is the capital of all Buddhas, the delight of all Buddhas;
it is the sublime palace of Bodhisattvas whose wisdom is free from doubt or obstruction;
it is the Great Merit Hall, adorned with all manner of subtle and exquisite ornaments, where the sound of the Dharma is constantly proclaimed.
He was accompanied by countless great bodhisattvas,
all of whom were true sons of the Tathāgata’s Dharma-body,
having gathered from various buddha-fields.
Surrounded on all sides by an immeasurable assembly of devas, humans, asuras, and arhats,
the World-Honored One then addressed the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, saying:
"Noble son, there is a dhāraṇī called 'The Heart of All Buddhas,' which has been spoken by as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges.
It is able to universally benefit all who are terrified."
If there are those who, with a sincere heart, receive, uphold, read, and recite [this],
they shall transcend the intense suffering of birth and death for hundreds of thousands of kalpas and will certainly attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
They will be able to practice swiftly and never regress until they attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment;
they shall never be born in vain in a world where no Buddha resides.
They constantly and skillfully comprehend all dhāraṇīs;
they always behold the Tathāgatas and draw near to make offerings to them;
and they constantly remember their past lives, having deep faith in cause and effect.
It can cause all harms and enmities from humans and non-humans in the present world to be eliminated;
illnesses shall not invade, and there shall be no premature deaths;
all evil demonic activities shall be utterly extinguished.
All evil karma will be eliminated without exception,
and all demonic armies will be struck with terror and disperse.
Son of good family, these are the letters, syllables, and phrases of this dhāraṇī.
This is that which is universally extolled by all Buddhas;
it is the very letters, phrases, and sentences of the Buddhas.
You should listen attentively to this dhāraṇī, which says:

When the Buddha had thus spoken this "Sarvaduṣṭāpātani Svāhā" dhāraṇī,
which is the heart-mantra of all Buddhas and possesses great majestic power, at that very moment,
the great earth and the great oceans of the trichiliocosm [trembled].
Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, shook in eighteen ways all at once;
the palaces of the devas were all tilted and shaken;
and the majestic splendor of the fierce and rebellious māra armies was extinguished.
They looked at one another in trepidation and terror, harboring deep anxiety.
At that time, all those throughout the three thousandfold world system who were ready for deliverance were startled by this sight and simultaneously cried out in distress.
Only those among the host of devas who placed their faith in the Triple Gem were filled with joy and leaped for gladness;
each of them took celestial flowers and scattered them from afar over the Buddha.
He also exhorted all the māras to take refuge in the Buddha-dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bodhisattvas:
"Out of compassion for all sentient beings, I shall now proclaim a dhāraṇī to enable them to be liberated from suffering and calamity."
"You should maintain correct mindfulness and proclaim this throughout the world,
so that all may receive, uphold, and attain supreme benefit and happiness.
At that time, the bodhisattvas and the rest of the assembly...
All were greatly rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Mind of All Buddhas.
